recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not reintroduce Appointment.order; any future adjustment to Appointment.basedOn target profiles should be handled under the later, specific Jira decisions governing those request references.
issue_request: FHIR-5698 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 PA change request saying Appointment.order could not work because Order was the wrong type for an Appointment fulfillment relationship. The approved resolution was to remove the Order property and leave any workable appointment order linkage for post-DSTU2 work.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by commit 13deffe106be55c50ae7473b96e95e0932129695, which changed the then-authoritative Appointment spreadsheet sources from Appointment.order to !Appointment.order. No additional Jira-keyed FHIR-5698 commit was found.
additional_context: Appointment is active in source/fhir.ini, while Order is listed under removed resources. Later request-linkage work, especially FHIR-13195 and FHIR-40634, evolved the replacement concept as Appointment.basedOn with concrete request target profiles rather than restoring Appointment.order.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. source/appointment/structuredefinition-Appointment.xml contains Appointment.basedOn with concrete request target profiles and no Appointment.order element, and the Appointment search parameter bundle uses based-on over Appointment.basedOn.

related_jiras.note: Implemented the post-DSTU2 request-linkage direction by renaming Appointment.incomingReferral to Appointment.basedOn for concrete request resources.
Later adjusted Appointment.basedOn target profiles without reviving Appointment.order.
